toolchain: leanprover/lean4:v4.34.0-rc2 (lean-toolchain); mathlib v4.34.0-rc2 and leanprover/comparator v4.34.0-rc2 per lakefile.toml
method: Blind source-level census over the project's own .lean files (git ls-files, .lean suffix, .lake/ excluded because it is the dependency tree: Mathlib, Comparator, and their transitive deps, not the project's code). A Python lexer tags every character as code / block-or-line comment (nested /- -/, /-- -/, /-! -/, --) / string literal, then every word-boundary occurrence of the 11 census keywords is classified by the tag at its position and attributed to the nearest preceding non-comment declaration header. Import closures are computed by BFS over `import X` lines from the root modules NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution and Euler.Solution (the solution_module of the two Comparator configs), expanding only modules that exist as project files; Mathlib.* imports are recorded as external leaves and not expanded. A second, lexer-free word-boundary grep (k2_rawcheck.py) was run as an independent cross-check of the counts, plus an os.walk file count to confirm git ls-files missed no on-disk .lean file. Neither lake nor lean was run; nothing was written under the tree. The four Comparator theorem names, challenge modules, and solution modules were read from ComparatorChallenges/*.json.
commands: git -C <tree> ls-files | grep '\.lean$' | grep -v '^\.lake/' | awk -F/ '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c
git -C <tree> ls-files | grep '\.lean$' | grep -v '^\.lake/' | xargs grep -n 'sorry'

sorry_summary: Five word-boundary occurrences of `sorry` in the project's .lean files: 4 in code, 1 in a comment, 0 in strings. The 4 code occurrences are exactly the proof bodies of the four Comparator challenge theorems in the two ComparatorChallenges/*.lean reference files. No `sorry` occurs anywhere under Euler/ or NavierStokes/ (1839 + 643 + 2 root files), in code, comment, or string. The raw grep cross-check gives the same 5 total.

No `axiom` declaration exists in the project's code. Note that `#print axioms` (4 lines, see print_axioms_commands) is not matched by the word-boundary regex because `axioms` is a different word.

native_decide.notes: no occurrence. The plain `decide` tactic (kernel-evaluated, does not add an axiom) appears ~201 times in code, e.g. `(by decide : 2 ≠ 0)`; it is not native_decide and is listed only for completeness.

macro.notes: no `macro` / `macro_rules` command. However `local notation` commands (which expand to macros) do occur in code, e.g. ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.lean:66,67,84, ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean, NavierStokes/ComparatorSolution.lean:13, Euler/Solution.lean; word-boundary `notation` matches 174 lines tree-wide including prose. These define surface syntax for EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) and divergence and cannot introduce axioms, but a source census cannot prove what any macro expands to.

additional_scans_not_in_the_gate_list.attribute: 26 lines, e.g. `attribute [local instance] ...`, `attribute [local irreducible] initialParent` — reducibility/instance attributes, not axioms

closure.how_computed: BFS over `^\s*import\s+(\S+)` lines starting at the root module, resolving module name M to file M.replace('.','/')+'.lean' among the 2486 tracked project files; modules without a project file (all Mathlib.*) are recorded as external leaves and not expanded. Membership means the module is transitively imported; it is necessary but not sufficient for the module's declarations to be used by any proof.

library_roots.NavierStokes.lean: imports NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution only; closure 581 project modules; contains ComparatorSolution: YES
library_roots.Euler.lean: imports Euler.EulerSingularity only; closure 1771 project modules; contains Euler.Solution: NO (Euler.Solution is nonetheless built by `lake build` because the Euler lean_lib glob `Euler.+` covers every Euler/*.lean module). Euler.Solution's closure (1829) is a strict superset of the Euler.lean root closure.

closure.the_four_sorry_files_vs_closures: Both sorry-bearing files (ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.lean, ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean) import only Mathlib and are imported by no project file. They are therefore in neither closure, and no declaration of the two solution modules can refer to them without an import, which would have shown in the BFS.

k1_axioms_verbatim.note: All three logs cover only the two NavierStokes theorems. None of them mentions the Euler pair (Euler.euler_breakdown_R3, Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity); the Euler side of this census therefore has no banked kernel counterpart in K1 and is reported as source-only.

cross_check_vs_k1.reasoning: K1's three runs each report exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for both exported NavierStokes theorems, with sorryAx absent. The source census predicts exactly this: (a) the only 4 code-level `sorry` are in ComparatorChallenges/*.lean, which import only Mathlib and are imported by nothing, so they cannot be in the dependency graph of NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 / _periodic as elaborated from NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution; (b) no `axiom`, `admit`, `native_decide` (which would surface as Lean.ofReduceBool), `implemented_by`, `extern`, `unsafe`, `opaque`, `set_option`, `macro`, or `elab` occurs in code in any of the 580 modules of the ComparatorSolution closure or anywhere else in the project; (c) the three axioms reported are the standard classical Mathlib trio, which the project's proofs inherit by using Mathlib. The axiom output and the census agree. Per the pre-registered rule, the axiom output WINS on any disagreement; there is none here, and had the kernel reported sorryAx, this census would have been reported as wrong (missing a sorry-introducing path), not the kernel. The Euler theorems are not in K1's logs, so for them the census is a prediction (no sorry / no extra axiom reachable) with no kernel result to cross-check against.

gate_answer: Gate (2) in its own terms: the project's .lean files (2486 outside .lake/, at HEAD 8937a8f4cbc7abaab5e9e97d1cc7f5d2319d9538) contain exactly 4 `sorry` in code — ComparatorChallenges/NavierStokes.lean:277 and :284 (theorems NavierStokes.Comparator.navier_stokes_breakdown_R3 and _periodic) and ComparatorChallenges/Euler.lean:88 and :184 (theorems Euler.euler_breakdown_R3 and Euler.exists_compact_smooth_euler_singularity) — plus one prose mention in a docstring. Each of the 4 is a Comparator challenge placeholder: the enclosing theorem is named in the corresponding ComparatorChallenges/*.json as a challenge theorem, the file's docstring calls the proofs intentional Comparator challenge placeholders, and the file imports only Mathlib. None is reachable from a main declaration by import: no project file imports any ComparatorChallenges.* module, so neither the 580-module import closure of NavierStokes.ComparatorSolution nor the 1829-module closure of Euler.Solution contains a sorry-bearing file. No axiom, admit, native_decide, implemented_by, extern, unsafe, opaque, set_option, macro, or elab occurs in code anywhere in the tree. Cross-checked against K1's banked `#print axioms` output (three runs, each [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] for both exported NavierStokes theorems, sorryAx absent): CONSISTENT. The axiom output wins on disagreement; there is no disagreement. The Euler pair has no K1 kernel counterpart and is source-only here. So the count IS four, as the gate wording presupposes, and the census confirms rather than contradicts the kernel.

what_this_does_not_establish: It is not a proof check; nothing here verifies that any theorem is true or that any proof term is kernel-valid.

A source census cannot detect an elaboration error, a proof that fails under the build, or an axiom introduced by a macro, tactic, or notation expansion; absence of the keywords in code is evidence, not proof, of absence in the elaborated environment.
Import-closure membership is necessary, not sufficient, for use by a proof; conversely, absence from the closure is what rules the four sorries out, and that part is solid at the source level.
It says nothing about the mathematical correctness of the paper, nor whether the Lean statements faithfully formalize Theorem 1.1 / Corollary 10.6 (statement fidelity is another unit's question).
The Euler pair is source-only: no banked kernel output for it was among my inputs.

The keyword list is the gate's; other axiom-relevant constructs (e.g. `Lean.ofReduceBool` via native_decide, `Classical` uses) are only covered insofar as they would show in `#print axioms`, which is K1's job.
